messages.2: Almost there: the number is close but outside tolerance. Usually it's rounding done too early, or an item included only halfway.
messages.3: The value is right in magnitude but has the opposite sign. Pick a convention (costs negative or costs positive) and stick to it across the whole model.
messages.4: The text doesn't match what's required.
messages.5: The logical value isn't the expected one.
messages.6: You typed the number by hand. The value is right but the level is failed: a hardcoded number doesn't update when the assumptions change, and it's the most common way to blow up a model in committee.
messages.7: The formula isn't pulling from the right cells. The result may even match by chance: what matters is that the link is there.
messages.8: There's a magic number inside the formula. Every parameter must sit in an assumption cell, visible and editable, not buried in the middle of a calculation.
messages.9: The anchors aren't the required ones. Without the right $ the formula stops working as soon as you copy it: that's the first test you put it through.
messages.10: The row isn't consistent: at least one cell contains a formula different from the others. It's the most common silent error in real models, because nobody sees it until it's too late.
messages.11: There's a circular reference where there shouldn't be one. Follow the chain of precedents to find where the loop closes.
messages.12: Here the circular reference is needed: interest depends on average debt, which depends on repayment, which depends on cash after interest. Turn on iterative calculation and close the loop.

messages.16: The colour coding isn't respected. Trade convention: hard-typed inputs in blue, formulas in black, links to other sheets in green. It lets whoever opens your file understand in three seconds what they can touch.

Privacy.testo:
## Who handles the data

Data controller: {titolare}. For any privacy request: {contatto}.

## In short

Bank Run is played without an account and without cookies. The site is hosted by Cloudflare, which sees technical data such as your IP address in order to deliver it and counts visits in aggregate. The more detailed **game statistics** are sent only if you have accepted them.

## What stays on your device

Your browser stores your game progress (completed levels, XP), your settings (audio, language, free play) and your choice about statistics. They are only used to make the game work, are not sent to anyone, and you can delete them at any time by clearing the site's data in your browser.

## Hosting and visit statistics (Cloudflare)

The site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages (Cloudflare, Inc.). To deliver the pages and protect them from abuse and attacks, Cloudflare processes the technical data of each request: IP address, browser and operating system type, page requested, date and time. This is necessary for the site to work (legal basis: legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

We also use **Cloudflare Web Analytics** to count visits in aggregate: number of visits, page views, country, referring site, device type. It uses no cookies, stores nothing on your device and creates no identifier that follows you across sites; we only see totals, never the individual person (legal basis: legitimate interest in knowing how much the site is used).

Cloudflare may process this data outside the European Union, with the safeguards required by the GDPR (EU-US Data Privacy Framework and standard contractual clauses).

## Game statistics (only with your consent)

If you answer "Yes" to the request, the game sends information about how it is played:

- levels opened, checked, completed or abandoned; attempts, times, keys pressed, hints used, tasks not passed; clicks on the author's profile link;
- language, game version, screen size, whether the screen is touch, browser language, the site you came from (domain name only) and the label of the link you opened, if any (for example “cv” in an address ending in ?ref=cv);
- any technical errors in the program.

Each browser is identified by a **random identifier** generated after your consent, not linked to your name or to any other data that identifies you. **Not** collected: name, email, IP address, cell contents or formulas you write.

**Why:** to understand which levels are too hard or unclear, how much the game is used, and to fix errors.

**Legal basis:** your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR and Art. 122 of the Italian Privacy Code). You can withdraw it at any time from **Settings**: from then on nothing more is sent and the identifier is deleted from your browser. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of what was collected before.

**Who receives the data:** PostHog Inc., which provides the statistics service as data processor, on servers in the European Union (Frankfurt, Germany). The data is not sold or used for advertising or profiling.

**How long:** at most 12 months, after which it is deleted.

## Fonts and other external services

All the game's files, fonts included, are served by the site itself: apart from Cloudflare and, if you accept them, the game statistics, opening Bank Run sends no data to other services.

## Your rights

You can request access, rectification, erasure, restriction of or objection to processing, and data portability (Arts. 15-22 GDPR) by writing to {contatto}. Since the data is linked only to the random identifier, include it in your request: you'll find it at the bottom of this page if you accepted statistics. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Italian Data Protection Authority (Garante per la protezione dei dati personali, www.garanteprivacy.it) or with the authority of your country.

## Children

If you are under 14, do not accept statistics: the game works exactly the same.

## Changes

Last updated: {data}. Any changes to this notice will be published here.
